rules.title: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act (Eviction Law)
rules.requirement: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only by court order on listed grounds, with notice to quit periods. Landlords who evict for personal occupancy or removal from residential use must meet post-eviction occupancy rules and face treble damages and civil penalties for violations.
rules.key_value: 3-day notice to quit for disorderly/destructive/rule violations; 3 months for at-will or year-to-year tenancies; 1 month for month-to-month; 90-day notice after foreclosure purchase
rules.penalty: Three times damages plus attorney fees and costs; civil penalty up to $10,000 per violation for improper residential use within five years after removal notice

requires.name: owner_occupied_two_three_family
requires.text: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings

coverage.summary: Applies to tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings in this section, within the broader eviction law.

rules.quoted_span: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only when a court issues an order for eviction.
